added_lines: Parish Newsletter 22nd November 2026 Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe No: 2071 Mt 25:31-46 Deacon Alex Ignat We are delighted to welcome Deacon Alex to Naas, Sallins and Two Mile House Parishes…. “My name is Ignat Alexandru Emanuel and I am from Romania. I am 24 years old and was ordained a deacon on 18th October 2026 by Bishop Iosif Păuleț . I have two wonderful parents and a little brother who is 13 years old. I entered the seminary at the age of 14 in 2016 and completed my studies in June this year. I enjoy doing lots of things, but what I love most is music. I will be serving as a deacon in Naas, assisting the Parish Team, until the end of May next year, when I return to Romania for my ordination to the priesthood. ” Advent begins ……. next weekend! As we enter the season of Advent, we are invited to pause, step out of the winter rush, and open our hearts to the quiet arrival of Christ Jesus. Beginning a new liturgical year invites us to watch with hope, even when the days feel short, dark and busy. Let us pray during these weeks with quiet trust and care for one another. May this Advent bring stillness, renewed faith, and warmth and light into our homes and parish family. This weekend, we highlight some opportunities for prayer and reflection. Spiritual helps which may allow us to celebrate the season of Advent with a sense of purpose and expectation, as we anticipate the birth of Christ at Christmas. Scripture Sharing, “Pathways in Advent” based on the Sunday Gospel: Tuesdays after 10am Mass in the Upper Room with Fr. Michael, starting on 24th November. Wednesdays after the 7pm Mass in the Day Chapel, Ballycane with Deacon Jody starting on 2nd December. Advent Giving We would like you to bring donations of non-perishable food or toiletries to Mass on Gaudete Sunday , which is 12th/13th December. These donations will be distributed by our Naas Point volunteers to those in need in the local area. Rorate Masses We invite you to our Special Christmas Preparation Masses starting on Thursday 17th December and finishing on 24th December. These Masses will take place at the earlier time of 7am. Summary of the Sallins Parish Accounts 2025 Dear Sallins Parishioners, Thank you for your continued generous support of both our basket and envelope collections which cover our day-to-day running expenses. The high envelope collection in 2024 was due to special collection in support of the Church refurbishment and is reflected in the high expenditure for that year in the Repairs and Maintenance Category. Both of these have now returned to normal levels. The rental income includes car park income and this is held in a separate account which did not transfer across before the year end in 2025. Tax Refund on your donations. The Parish qualifies for this scheme and is entitled to reclaim tax at a rate of 45% on donations of more than €250 per year. Some tax refund authorisation mandates have now expired and we would be delighted if you could sign up again for another 5-year period. To take advantage of this form, you would need to donate in a traceable way, the easiest of which is through the weekly envelope boxes which will be available soon for 2027. Expenditure: The legal and professional fees in 2024 related to the sale of the land plot to the rear of the Parish Centre. I am pleased to report that the sale was finalised this year and our accounts for 2026 will reflect this along with the expenditure incurred for the church roof replacement and parish centre upgrade. We are also planning to upgrade the church heating system quite soon. Thank You! Once again for your continued and generous support to our finances – it is very much appreciated. Notes on the 2025 Accounts Income from all sources remained strong in 2025, particularly from the shrines.

The income from the car park which is included in the Rental income category has increased significantly since the teachers from the Mercy Convent started to park in their own grounds, freeing up more space in the car park.
Also, the shop income continues to go from strength to strength, thank you to all our customers.
The First (Development) Collection goes to the upkeep of the Churches and other parish buildings and will be used to cover the upcoming building work on the Parish Office and new Parish Centre.
The Second (Offertory) Collection covers the day-to-day costs of running the parish, e.g. energy costs, staff wages, running costs for the parish offices and shops, etc.
This figure is the net income for Naas Point , which is our parish ‘outreach’ that seeks to look after those who are vulnerable and struggling to make ends meet.

Expenditure Tight control of spending in spite of increased prices has resulted in the total expenditure for the year coming in slightly less than in 2024. An increase in the total for the Repairs and Maintenance category was due to the improvements to the lighting both inside and outside Ballycane Church and some initial expenditure relating to the building work for the new Parish Centre on the Sallins Road.

The spend on Computer Software etc has returned to normal levels after the purchase of the large screens for Ballycane Church and some extra screens for the Parish Church in 2024. Payments to Priests The priests of the parish are paid from the seven specific collections spread throughout the year including the ones at Christmas and Easter.
They are not paid from the Development or Offertory Collections.
Their wages are fixed by the diocese at €25,200 for Parish Priests and €24,000 for Curates.
Parish Lotto Thank you very much to everyone who takes part in the parish lotto and particularly to the promotors and the Lotto Committee, led tirelessly by Jo Coy.

It is an important element of the parish finances and we encourage you to take part whether online, with an annual ticket, standing order or by purchasing a ticket for €2 in one of the participating outlets around Naas.
Tap & Go This year saw new Tap & Go machines in the two Naas Churches.
These machines have the added benefit that you may input your details after making a donation and that makes your donation traceable to you.

Although it may take you a minute to fill out your details, you do only have to do it once and the machine will remember your card and when you return to that machine, it will not ask you to input your details again and we will automatically know that it was you making another donation.
Please note that this will only work if you return to the same machine each time.

Tax Refund on your Donations to Naas Parish Once you have made a donation to the parish in a way that we can trace, whether it is the Tap & Go machine as described above, an online donation, a weekly envelope where you have written your name and address on the first few which you use, you can allow us to claim an additional 45% of your donation by filling out a form and returning it to the Parish Office.
This money is returned to us by Revenue and there is no cost to yourself.
This facility is available if your total donations for the year add up to over €250 which includes donations to the priests, special collections, Naas Point as well as the regular weekly collections.
Please do call into the Parish Office to find out more.
It makes a significant difference to Parish Finances and we can only do it with your help.
And finally, … thank you very much to everyone, our finances are healthy because of your generosity and that of all the parishioners here in Naas, thank you for your continued support of our parish.
